<reason>PRO won by holding the debate to the comparative motion ("more affordable," not "affordable") and exploiting two CON slips: "earlier legalization would have changed skylines" and "trims prices a few percent." CON's rescue—that the few percent was an arguendo ceiling and the honest estimate is zero—required an effectively horizontal demand curve (every new unit absorbed by an arrival who otherwise would not have come), and PRO's vacancy/renewal-letter mechanism plus the Houston-versus-San-Francisco observation made that position hard to hold. CON's strongest material (the 2008 timeline, Miami, the land-repricing answer to Q2, and the "immunized claim" charge) was genuinely sharp and kept the debate competitive, but its weighing rested on the national rate surge, which PRO correctly noted is baseline in both worlds and cannot decide a counterfactual comparison. CON's closing line "same world with cranes" was memorable but asserted rather than demonstrated that twenty years of extra units house nobody at lower rents. Both sides answered pressure questions directly with proper A1/A2 format; PRO's minor clipping cost little. Grounding on both sides was ordinary background knowledge without fake precision.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's Rebuttal 2 handling of Miami—reading CON's own "glut, bust, foreclosed towers" as supply crushing prices, then separating the later foreign-capital demand shock and noting the missing no-build counterfactual—neutralized CON's best counterexample, while pinning CON's "few percent" line as the motion conceded forced CON into the implausible "roughly zero" position for the rest of the debate.</best_rebuttal>
